[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 24.1] (4) The appellant must serve on the adjudicator and the Chief Land Registrar a copy of the appeal court’s decision on the appeal as soon as reasonably practicable and in any event within 14 days of receipt by the appellant of the appeal court’s decision. ## Appeals under the Merchant Shipping Act 1995

## 25.1

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 25.1] (1) his paragraph applies to appeals under the Merchant Shipping Act 1995 and for this purpose a re-hearing and an application under section 61 of the Merchant Shipping Act 1995 are treated as appeals. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 25.1] (2) The appellant must file any report to the Secretary of State containing the decision from which the appeal is brought with the appellant’s notice. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 25.1] (3) Where a re-hearing by the High Court is ordered under sections 64 or 269 of the Merchant Shipping Act 1995, the Secretary of State must give reasonable notice to the parties whom he considers to be affected by the re-hearing. ## 26.1

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 26.1] In an appeal to the Planning Court or an application for permission to appeal to the Planning Court the provisions of Practice Direction 54D must be followed. ## Appeals from decisions of the Law Society or the Solicitors Disciplinary Tribunal to the High Court

## 27.1

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 27.1] (1) This paragraph applies to appeals from the Law Society or the Solicitors Disciplinary Tribunal (‘the Tribunal’) to the High Court under the Solicitors Act 1974, Administration of Justice Act 1985, the Courts and Legal Services Act 1990, the European Communities (Lawyer’s Practice) Regulations 2000 or the European Communities (Recognition of Professional Qualifications) Regulations 2015. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 27.1] (2) The appellant must file the appellant’s notice in the Administrative Court. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 27.1] (3) Unless the court otherwise orders the appellant must serve the appellant’s notice on –

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 27.1] (a) every party to the proceedings before the Tribunal; and

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 27.1] (b) the Law Society. ## Appeals from decisions of the Bar Standards Board or Disciplinary Tribunals to the High Court

## 27.1A

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 27.1A] (1) This paragraph applies to appeals to the High Court under section 24 of the Crime and Courts Act 2013—

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 27.1A] (a) from decisions of the Bar Standards Board on review under the Bar Qualification Rules; or

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 27.1A] (b) from decisions of Disciplinary Tribunals of the Council of the Inns of Court. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 27.1A] (2) The appellant must file the appellant’s notice in the Administrative Court. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 27.1A] (3) Unless the court otherwise orders, the appellant must serve the appellant’s notice on—

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 27.1A] (a) every party to the proceedings before the Bar Standards Board or the Disciplinary Tribunal as appropriate; and

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 27.1A] (b) the Council of the Inns of Court in the case of appeals from decisions of the Disciplinary Tribunal. ## APPEALS TO THE HIGH COURT – WALES ONLY

## Welsh statutory appeals

## Introduction

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Introduction] 27A.1 (1) This paragraph and paragraphs 27A.2 to 27A.7 apply to certain appeals to the High Court under enactments relating to Wales only (“Welsh statutory appeals”). (2) For these purposes, Welsh statutory appeals are appeals under the following enactments— (a) section 79 of the Local Government Act 2000; (b) section 32(1) of the Education (Wales) Act 2014; and (c)  any of sections 59, 97, 101 or 105 of the Welsh Language (Wales) Measure 2011. ## Service of documents in a Welsh statutory appeal to be by parties

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Service of documents in a Welsh statutory appeal to be by parties] 27A.2 The Administrative Court will not serve documents in a Welsh statutory appeal, and service must be effected by the parties as provided in the following paragraphs. ## Appellant’s notice in a Welsh statutory appeal

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Appellant’s notice in a Welsh statutory appeal] 27A.3 (1) The appellant must file the appellant’s notice in the Administrative Court Office of the High Court at the District Registry in Cardiff. (2) If the appellant’s notice is filed at an Administrative Court Office other than in Cardiff the proceedings will be transferred to Cardiff. (3) The appellant must file the appellant’s notice — (a) within the time specified in the relevant statutory provision listed in paragraph 27A.1; or (b) if the relevant statutory provision specifies no time, within 28 days of the date of the decision the appellant wishes to appeal. (4) The appellant must file with the appellant’s notice— (a) a statement of facts relied on and grounds for bringing the appeal; (b) a copy of the decision the appellant wishes to appeal; (c) any written evidence in support of the appeal. (5) The appellant must— (a) within 7 days of the date on which the appeal was filed, serve a sealed copy of the appellant’s notice and the documents in sub-paragraph (4) on— (i) the authority or tribunal which made the decision the appellant wishes to appeal; and (ii) the respondent to the appeal, and (b) file a certificate of service confirming the date of service under sub-paragraph (a). ## Respondent’s notice in a Welsh statutory appeal

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Respondent’s notice in a Welsh statutory appeal] 27A.4 If the respondent intends to contest the appeal the respondent must, within 21 days of service under paragraph 27A.3(5)(a), file — (a) a respondent’s notice; (b) any written evidence in contesting the appeal. ## Time of permission hearing in a Welsh statutory appeal

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Time of permission hearing in a Welsh statutory appeal] 27A.5 Where the relevant statutory provision requires the appellant to obtain the permission of the Court to appeal, a permission hearing will be listed no earlier than 7 days after the expiry of the time limit in paragraph 27A.4. ## Listing of a Welsh statutory appeal

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Listing of a Welsh statutory appeal] 27A.6 Unless the Court orders otherwise, the appeal will not be heard earlier than 28 days after the later of— (a) the expiry of the time limit in paragraph 27A.4; or (b) if applicable, the date on which permission to appeal is granted. ## Further Documentation for hearing of a Welsh statutory appeal

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Further Documentation for hearing of a Welsh statutory appeal] 27A.7 (1)  Sub-paragraphs (2) to (4) apply only where permission to appeal has been granted or where permission is not required. (2) The appellant must, not less than 21 days before the date of the hearing of the appeal, file— (a) a paginated and indexed bundle of the appellant’s and respondent’s notices and the documents filed with them; and (b) a skeleton argument. (3) The respondent and any other party wishing to make representations at the hearing of the appeal must file a skeleton argument not less than 14 days before the date of the hearing of the appeal. (4) The appellant must file a paginated and indexed bundle of all statutory materials and case law relied upon by the appellant and the respondent not less than 7 days before the hearing of the appeal. ## APPEALS TO THE COUNTY COURT

## Appeals under sections 204 and 204A of the Housing Act 1996

## 28.1

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 28.1] (1) An appellant should include appeals under section 204 and section 204A of the Housing Act 1996 in one appellant’s notice. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 28.1] (2) If it is not possible to do so (for example because an urgent application under section 204A is required) the appeals may be included in separate appellant’s notices. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 28.1] (3) An appeal under section 204A may include an application for an order under section 204A(4)(a) requiring the authority to secure that accommodation is available for the applicant’s occupation. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 28.1] (4) If, exceptionally, the court makes an order under section 204A(4)(a) without notice, the appellant’s notice must be served on the authority together with the order. Such an order will normally require the authority to secure that accommodation is available until a hearing date when the authority can make representations as to whether the order under section 204A(4)(a) should be continued. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 28.1] (5) Unless the court orders otherwise –

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 28.1] (a) the appellant shall file and serve its proposed case management directions for the appeal together with the appellant’s notice;

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 28.1] (b) the respondent shall within 14 days thereafter either agree those directions or file and serve alternative proposed directions;

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 28.1] (c) within 14 days after service of the appellant’s notice the respondent must disclose any documents relevant to the decision under appeal, in so far as not previously disclosed;

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 28.1] (d) within 14 days after receipt of any documents disclosed under sub-paragraph (c) the appellant may make any amendments to its grounds of appeal which arise out of those documents. ## Appeal under Part II of the Immigration and Asylum Act 1999 (carriers’ liability)

## 29.1

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 29.1] (1) A person appealing to the County Court under section 35A or section 40B of the Immigration and Asylum Act 1999 (‘the Act’) against a decision by the Secretary of State to impose a penalty under section 32 or a charge under section 40 of the Act must, subject to sub-paragraph (2), file the appellant’s notice within 28 days after receiving the penalty notice or charge notice. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 29.1] (2) Where the appellant has given notice of objection to the Secretary of State under section 35(4) or section 40A(3) of the Act within the time prescribed for doing so, the appellant must file the appellant’s notice within 28 days after receiving notice of the Secretary of State’s decision in response to the notice of objection. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 29.1] (3) Sections 35A and 40B of the Act provide that any appeal under those sections shall be a re-hearing of the Secretary of State’s decision to impose a penalty or charge, and therefore rule 52.21(1) does not apply. ## Local Government (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 1976

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Local Government (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 1976] 30.1 Where one of the grounds upon which an appeal against a notice under sections 21, 23 or 35 of the Local Government (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 1976 is brought is that –

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Local Government (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 1976] (a) it would have been fairer to serve the notice on another person; or

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Local Government (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 1976] (b) that it would be reasonable for the whole or part of the expenses to which the appeal relates to be paid by some other person,

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Local Government (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 1976] that person must be made a respondent to the appeal, unless the court, on application of the appellant made without notice, otherwise directs. ## 31.1

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 31.1] (1) This paragraph applies in relation to an appeal against a decision of a registration officer, being a decision referred to in—

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 31.1] (a) section 56(1) of the Representation of the People Act 1983 (“the Act”);

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 31.1] (b) article 5(1) of the National Assembly for Wales (Representation of the People) Order 2007 (“the 2007 Order”); or

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 31.1] (c) regulation 74(1) of the Recall of MPs Act 2015 (Recall Petition) Regulations 2016 (“the 2016 Regulations”). [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 31.1] (2) Where a person (“the appellant”) has given notice of such an appeal in accordance with the relevant requirements of—

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 31.1] (a) section 56, and the regulations made under section 53 (“the 2001 Regulations”) of the Act;

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 31.1] (b) article 5 of, and paragraph 9 of Schedule 1 to, the 2007 Order; or

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 31.1] (c) regulations 74 and 77 of the 2016 Regulations, the registration officer must, within 7 days after receiving the notice, forward by post to the County Court—

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 31.1] (i) the notice; and

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 31.1] (ii) the statement required by the 2001 Regulations, by paragraph 9 of Schedule 1 to the 2007 Order or by regulation 77 of the 2016 Regulations as the case may be. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 31.1] (3) The respondents to the appeal will be –

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 31.1] (a) the registration officer; and

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 31.1] (b) if the decision of the registration officer was given in favour of any other person than the appellant, that other person. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 31.1] (4) On the hearing of the appeal–

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 31.1] (a) the statement forwarded to the court by the registration officer, and any document containing information submitted to the court by the registration officer pursuant to the 2001 Regulations, 2007 Order and 2016 Regulations, are admissible as evidence of the facts stated in them; and

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 31.1] (b) the court –

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 31.1] (i) may draw any inference of fact that the registration officer might have drawn; and

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 31.1] (ii) may give any decision and make any order that the registration officer ought to have given or made. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 31.1] (5) A respondent to an appeal (other than the registration officer) is not liable for nor entitled to costs, unless he appears before the court in support of the registration officer’s decision. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 31.1] (6) Rule 52.12 (appellant’s notice) does not apply to an appeal to which this paragraph applies. ## 31.2

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 31.2] (1) In this paragraph –

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 31.2] (a) ‘anonymous entry’ has the meaning given by section 9B(4) of the Representation of the People Act 1983;

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 31.2] (b) ‘appeal notice’ means the notice required by regulation 32 of the Representation of the People (England and Wales) Regulations 2001. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 31.2] (2) This paragraph applies to an appeal to the County Court to which paragraph 31.1 (Representation of the People Act 1983 – appeals against decisions of registration officers) applies if a party to the appeal is a person –

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 31.2] (a) whose entry in the register is an anonymous entry; or

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 31.2] (b) who has applied for such an entry. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 31.2] (3) This paragraph also applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal from a decision of the County Court in an appeal to which paragraph 31.1 applies. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 31.2] (4) The appellant may indicate in the appeal notice that an application for an anonymous entry has been applied for, or that the entry in the register is an anonymous entry. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 31.2] (5) The respondent or any other person who applies to become a party to the proceedings may indicate in a respondent’s notice or an application to join the proceedings that the entry in the register is an anonymous entry, or that an application has been made for an anonymous entry. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 31.2] (6) Where the appellant gives such an indication in the appeal notice, the court will refer the matter to a District Judge for directions about the further conduct of the proceedings, and, in particular, directions about how the matter should be listed in the court list. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 31.2] (7) Where the court otherwise becomes aware that a party to the appeal is a person referred to in sub-paragraph (2), the court will give notice to the parties that no further step is to be taken until the court has given any necessary directions for the further conduct of the matter. ## 31.3

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 31.3] (1) Where two or more appeals under—

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 31.3] (a) section 56, and the 2001 Regulations;

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 31.3] (b) article 5 of, and paragraph 9 of Schedule 1 to, the 2007 Order; or

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 31.3] (c) regulations 74 and 77 of the 2016 Regulations,

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 31.3] involve the same point of law, the court may direct that one appeal (“the test-case appeal”) is to be heard first as a test case. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 31.3] (2) The court will send a notice of the direction to each party to all of those appeals. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 31.3] (3) Where a notice under sub-paragraph (2) is served on any party to an appeal (other than the test-case appeal), that party may (within 7 days after the notice is served on that party) give notice to the court requesting the appeal to be heard and–

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 31.3] (a) the court will hear that appeal after the test-case appeal is disposed of;

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 31.3] (b) the court will give the parties to that appeal notice of the day on which it will be heard; and

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 31.3] (c) the party who gave the notice is not entitled to receive any costs of the separate hearing of that appeal unless the judge otherwise orders. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 31.3] (4) Where no notice is given under sub-paragraph (3) within the period limited by that paragraph –

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 31.3] (a) the decision on the test-case appeal binds the parties to each of the other appeals;

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 31.3] (b) without further hearing, the court will make, in each other appeal, an order similar to the order in the test-case appeal; and

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 31.3] (c) the party to each other appeal who is in the same interest as the unsuccessful party to the selected appeal is liable for the costs of the test-case appeal in the same manner and to the same extent as the unsuccessful party to that appeal and an order directing the party to pay such costs may be made and enforced accordingly. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 31.3] (5) Sub-paragraph (4)(a) does not affect the right to appeal to the Court of Appeal of any party to an appeal other than the test-case appeal. ## Appeals under section 11 of the UK Borders Act 2007

## 32.1

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 32.1] (1) A person appealing to the County Court under section 11 of the UK Borders Act 2007 (‘the Act’) against a decision by the Secretary of State to impose a penalty under section 9(1) of the Act, must, subject to sub-paragraph (2), file the appellant’s notice within 28 days after receiving the penalty notice. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 32.1] (2) Where the appellant has given notice of objection to the Secretary of State under section 10 of the Act within the time prescribed for doing so, the appellant’s notice must be filed within 28 days after receiving notice of the Secretary of State’s decision in response to the notice of objection. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 32.1] Updated: Saturday, 6 April 2024
